name: sco2_recompression_brayton
title: Supercritical CO2 recompression Brayton cycle (100 MW net)
summary: Design-point sCO2 recompression Brayton cycle with two 10-section recuperators after the TESPy model-library example, validated against the published state and exergy table of Penkuhn & Tsatsaronis (2018): turbomachinery at isentropic efficiency, recuperators at 5 K lower terminal temperature difference, net power imposed at 100 MW, recompressed fraction fixed by equal merge temperatures.

authors: Francesco Witte (TESPy model and sCO2_exergy original)
origin.course: TESPy model library sCO2 example (commit 19425523); original model github.com/fwitte/sCO2_exergy (Witte et al. 2022); validation data Penkuhn & Tsatsaronis (2018)

verification.summary: Compared with a TESPy run of sco2.ipynb: 69 common variables, 0 differ at rtol=0.001, max 4.3e-4 on UA_rec1 (smoothed vs standard LMTD). Against the published Penkuhn & Tsatsaronis (2018) state table: 48 values, 0 differ, max 7.5e-4 on e_T[5] (rounded published values).
verification.reference: TESPy run of docs/model_library/sco2.ipynb (commit 19425523, venv, TESPy 0.11.3.dev0/CoolProp): 69 common variables 0 differ (rtol=0.001); published Penkuhn & Tsatsaronis (2018) state table (T, p, thermal and mechanical exergy of the 12 states): 48 values, 0 differ (rtol=0.001)
verification.notes: Max rel. diff. 4.3e-4 vs the TESPy run (UA_rec1, TESPy smoothed LMTD vs standard LMTD) and 7.5e-4 vs the published table (e_T[5], published values rounded to 2 decimals). T and p of all 12 states within 0.19 K / 1e-4 rel. of the publication, the same deviations as the TESPy run itself (CoolProp version).

history.action: added (T-TRANSLATE of the TESPy sCO2 recompression Brayton example)
